items.title: Section: Withholding the Truth from Someone Chasing Happiness the Wrong Way

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，見諸有情為求現法後法事故，廣行非理，懷嫌恨心、懷恚惱心，不為宣說如實正理，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。若由懶惰懈怠所蔽，不為宣說，非染違犯。無違犯者，若自無知；若無氣力；若轉請他有力者說；若即彼人自有智力；若彼有餘善友攝受；若欲方便調彼、伏彼，廣說如前；若知為說如實正理，起嫌恨心，若發惡言，若顛倒受，若無愛敬；若復知彼性弊𢤱悷；不為宣說，皆無違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who see beings pursuing happiness in this life or the next through genuinely mistaken methods, and who, gripped by resentment or hostility, withhold the true teaching that would set them straight, commit a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. If mere laziness or indolence keeps them from teaching, it is a non-tainted violation. ... There is no violation: for one who genuinely does not know the correct teaching themselves; who lacks the strength to teach; who redirects a more capable teacher instead; when the person already has sufficient wisdom of their own; when the person already has another genuine spiritual friend guiding them; when withholding the teaching itself serves as skilful means, as described more fully earlier; when the bodhisattva knows in advance that offering the true teaching would only provoke resentment, harsh speech, wilful distortion, or open contempt; or when the bodhisattva knows the person's very nature is base and hard to free from desire, or fierce, unruly, and hard to tame.

items.title: Section: Failing to Repay a Genuine Debt of Gratitude

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，於先有恩諸有情所不知恩惠、不了恩惠，懷嫌恨心，不欲現前如應酬報，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。若為嬾惰懈怠所蔽，不現酬報，非染違犯。無違犯者，勤加功用，無力無能不獲酬報；若欲方便調彼、伏彼，廣說如前；若欲報恩而彼不受；皆無違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who, towards beings who have shown them genuine kindness in the past, fail to truly recognise that kindness or keep it clearly in mind, and, gripped by resentment, are unwilling to repay it directly and as circumstances call for, commit a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. If mere laziness or indolence keeps them from repaying it, it is a non-tainted violation. ... There is no violation for one who has genuinely applied real effort but simply lacks the capacity to repay the kindness; who withholds repayment purely as a skilful means to guide the other, as described more fully earlier; or who genuinely wishes to repay the kindness but finds the other person unwilling to accept it.

items.title: Section: Refusing to Console the Grieving

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，見諸有情墮在喪失財寶、眷屬、祿位、難處，多生愁惱，懷嫌恨心，不往開解，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。若為懶惰懈怠所蔽，不往開解，非染違犯。無違犯者，應知如前於他事業不為助伴。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who see beings caught in the hardship of losing their wealth, family, or position, sunk in real grief, and who, gripped by resentment, refuse to go and console them, commit a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. If mere laziness or indolence keeps them away, it is a non-tainted violation. ... The no-fault conditions here should be understood exactly as in the earlier precept on not lending a hand with another's undertaking.

items.title: Section: Withholding Material Support from Genuine Need — and Ven. Miao-Jing's Atomic Bomb

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，有飲食等資生眾具，見有求者來正悕求飲食等事，懷嫌恨心、懷恚惱心，而不給施，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。若由懶惰、懈怠、放逸，不能施與，非染違犯。無違犯者，若現無有可施財物；若彼悕求不如法物、所不宜物；若欲方便調彼、伏彼，廣說如前；若來求者王所匪宜，將護王意；若護僧制；而不惠施，皆無違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who possess food, clothing, and other necessities of life, and who, when someone genuinely in need comes seeking such things, refuse to give out of resentment or hostility, commit a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. If mere laziness, indolence, or negligence prevents the giving, it is a non-tainted violation. ... There is no violation: when the bodhisattva simply has nothing available to give; when what is requested is an improper or genuinely unsuitable object; when withholding serves as a skilful means to guide the person, as described more fully earlier; when giving the requested item would run contrary to the ruling authority's own prohibition, out of respect for that authority; or when withholding upholds a rule the monastic community has properly established.

items.title: Section: Properly Caring for One's Own Students — Teaching, Provisioning, and Screening Out False Seekers

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，攝受徒眾，懷嫌恨心，而不隨時無倒教授、無倒教誡；知眾匱乏，而不為彼從諸淨信長者、居士、婆羅門等，如法追求衣服、飲食、諸坐臥具、病緣醫藥資身什物，隨時供給；是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。若由懶惰、懈怠、放逸，不往教授、不往教誡、不為追求如法眾具，非染違犯。無違犯者，若欲方便調彼、伏彼，廣說如前；若護僧制；若有疹疾；若無氣力，不任加行；若轉請餘有勢力者；若知徒眾世所共知，有大福德，各自有力求衣服等資身眾具；若隨所應教授教誡，皆已無倒教授教誡；若知眾內有本外道，為竊法故來入眾中，無所堪能，不可調伏；皆無違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who take on students or dependents, but, gripped by resentment, fail to give them timely, correct instruction and correction, and, knowing they lack what they need, fail to properly seek clothing, food, bedding, and medical care for them from faithful patrons — this constitutes a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. If mere laziness, indolence, or negligence is the cause, it is a non-tainted violation. ... There is no violation: when withholding serves as skilful means, as described more fully earlier; when it upholds the monastic community's own rule; when the bodhisattva is themselves ill or lacks the strength; when a more capable person is asked to take over instead; when the student is already well known to be independently well provided for; when proper instruction and correction have already been fully given; or when the bodhisattva recognises that a particular person has joined the community as a disguised outsider purely to steal the teaching, genuinely incapable of benefiting and impossible to actually guide.

items.title: Section: Accommodating Others' Wishes — But Only When It Actually Serves Them

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，懷嫌恨心，於他有情不隨心轉，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。若由懶惰、懈怠、放逸，不隨其轉，非染違犯。無違犯者，若彼所愛非彼所宜；若有疾病；若無氣力，不任加行；若護僧制；若彼所愛雖彼所宜，而於多眾非宜、非愛；若為降伏諸惡外道；若欲方便調彼、伏彼，廣說如前；不隨心轉，皆無違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who, gripped by resentment, refuse to go along with another being's wishes commit a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. If mere laziness, indolence, or negligence is the cause, it is a non-tainted violation. ... There is no violation: when what the person desires, though genuinely wanted, is not actually good for them; when the bodhisattva is ill or lacks the strength; when it upholds the monastic community's own rule; when what the person desires, though good for them individually, would be unsuitable or unwelcome to the wider community; when refusing serves to subdue genuinely harmful outsiders; or when refusing serves as skilful means to guide the person, as described more fully earlier.

blocks.text: More precepts on benefiting beings. Each has its exceptions, which show what the precept is for.

Seeing beings pursue happiness "through mistaken methods", and not explaining the right way, out of resentment. Master Cháng Bǎi gives examples of ascetic practices of his era: throwing things into fire as "the mouth of the gods", standing naked.
Failing to recognise and repay past kindness. No offence for one who tries but lacks means.
Refusing to comfort those grieving over lost wealth, family, or position.

Refusing food or clothing to someone in need. No offence "when one has nothing to give", or "when what is sought is improper". Master Cháng Bǎi's modern example: a bodhisattva who knew how to build an atomic bomb should not give that away.

Taking on students, but failing out of resentment to instruct and correct them, or to provide for them; "in taking on students one must provide both Dharma and food" (Master Cháng Bǎi). No offence if one learns that someone joined only "to steal the teaching" for an outside school.

Refusing to go along with another's wishes out of resentment is an offence, but only when going along "actually serves them". Venerable Miào Jìng: helping someone get rich is what they want, but if they would then do every wrong, it is not help.

quiz.q: Seeing beings pursue this life's or the next life's welfare through wrong methods, a bodhisattva who out of resentment does not explain the truth — what is this?
quiz.why: Withholding the true teaching out of resentment is tainted; from laziness, untainted. Master Cháng Bǎi: this item concerns kind speech — failing to teach beings.

quiz.q: What examples of "wrong methods" does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: thinking fire is the gods' mouth and burning offerings; nakedness, standing on one leg, eating a single sesame seed — pointless austerities
reciting and bowing to the Buddha
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: believing fire is the mouth of the gods and throwing things into it; going naked, standing on one leg, eating a single sesame seed or grain of wheat — pointless austerities. Removing evil karma requires cutting off afflictions. Venerable Miào Jìng: "sacrificial outsiders" make offerings to the gods.

quiz.q: The English renders "bù liǎo" as "fail to acknowledge" and "xiànqián rúyìng chóubào" as "repay as circumstances call for." What do the lectures say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: "bù liǎo" means failing to remember clearly; Miào Jìng: "xiànqián" means repaying in person, not through an intermediary — the English loses both
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: not clearly remembering is "bù liǎo," which becomes ingratitude. Venerable Miào Jìng: "xiànqián" means repaying the benefactor in person, without an intermediary. The English drops both senses.

quiz.q: The English renders this as losing "wealth, family, position, or standing." How do the lectures read "nán chù"?
options: only three losses — wealth, family, position; "nán chù" is the hardship of being in such loss
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: fallen into the hardship of losing wealth, family, or position. Venerable Miào Jìng: losses of wealth, family, and position — these three sufferings. The English adds a fourth item, "standing."

quiz.q: Which is an exemption when a bodhisattva does not give requested necessities?
options: the person seeks something improper or unsuitable
quiz.why: No violation when one has nothing to give, "when what is sought is improper or unsuitable," when withholding as skilful means, when the request is against the ruler's wishes, or to protect the monastic rules. Master Cháng Bǎi: improper objects such as mahjong tables or drugs.

quiz.q: Both lectures use an "atomic bomb" example. How does each use it?
options: Cháng Bǎi: if a bodhisattva were the father of the atomic bomb, they would not give away that knowledge — a weapon of mass killing and a state secret; Miào Jìng: under "against the ruler's wishes," someone planning rebellion asks the bodhisattva for a nuclear bomb
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: suppose a bodhisattva were the father of the atomic bomb, able to give away that knowledge — it is a weapon of mass killing and a state secret. Venerable Miào Jìng, under "against the ruler's wishes": perhaps someone plotting rebellion asks the bodhisattva for a nuclear bomb.

quiz.q: Among the exemptions for caring for students, what kind of person in the group need not be instructed?
options: a former outsider who joined only to steal the teaching, incapable and untamable
quiz.why: No violation "if one knows that among the group is a former outsider who joined only to steal the teaching, incapable and untamable." Master Cháng Bǎi: an outsider stealing the dharma is called "dwelling as a thief."
